# Task 12E2E2A: global admitted-work scheduler authority

## Fix round 1: shared scan lock order

This section supersedes the original scheduler64 source identity below. The original implementation and its complete test record remain intact.

Fix base: `8e8358dc13b2e3ae6f103055a6a44eddcb91ff11`. The independent review in `task-12e2e2a-review.md` found one Important concurrency defect: scheduler64's materialized run scan could lock organizations A then B while worker63's materialized expired-dispatch scan locked B then A. Sorting the classified output does not sort the earlier locking function calls. The two scans had different global advisory locks, so each could hold one organization lock and wait on the other. This is an internal database deadlock between trusted extension functions.

I read the review in full, applied receiving-code-review and systematic-debugging, and used strict TDD for the correction. The hypothesis was specific: a shared outer scan lock must prevent the cycle without changing the selected work or any caller authority. Two authentic unchanged-production runs reproduced SQLSTATE `40P01`; only then did production change.

The fix adds one `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('ordered-worker63-dispatch',0))` at the start of scheduler64 claim's locking path, before `ordered-scheduler64-selection`, replay, expired-history maintenance, and all organization inspection. Nothing in worker63, public62, release61, the dormant runtime, grants, request shapes, or mutation logic changed. Heartbeat, finish, and abandon still derive exactly one tenant/run from the retained schedule and retain their previous selection-lock protocol. They do not acquire the new outer dispatch lock.

The new PostgreSQL test uses two real public62 triggers in A/B order, enables reviewed pricing for B first, and creates B/A planning dispatches through worker63. Both runs use reviewed release61 prepare/start/result/settlement/artifact/admission; public62 approval advances B after A's admission. The test asserts opposite physical row orders and waits for the actual recorded dispatch deadline. No owner update changes any predecessor or expiry. A read-only owner transaction holds B's budget row. Worker63 recovery takes its real global and B-organization locks, then blocks on that row; `pg_blocking_pids` proves that boundary before scheduler64 begins. A second observed blocker proves scheduler64 reached the overlapping scan boundary. Releasing the budget row deterministically formed the old lock cycle. There is no timing sleep to induce overlap. The only timer waits for actual lease expiry.

With the fix, the same observed barrier shows scheduler64 waiting on worker63's global dispatch lock before acquiring its own selection or organization locks. Recovery hands off A's approval pause and leaves B's admitted work intact; scheduling selects B once, exact replay is stable, both planning jobs/admissions remain retained, and no duplicate schedule appears. An unchanged-behavior check then holds the dispatch lock and verifies owned heartbeat and pre-effect abandon can complete without it.

Behavioral RED commands: `node /tmp/zasp-scheduler64-fix1.9asP0D/run.mjs red-worker-lock go test ./apiserver -count=1 -run '^TestSecurityAgentScheduler64WorkerRecoveryLockOrderPostgres$' -timeout 5m -v`, then the identical command with label `red-worker-lock-repeat`. The scheduler returned `ERROR: deadlock detected (SQLSTATE 40P01)` both times, while worker63 completed. Go package times were 52.885s and 52.202s; wall times were 60.306s and 57.914s. This was a product RED, not a fixture/setup failure.

The registration calibration printed fingerprint `9a8a090c97a4c8b913921dd1503b6ca0925c837adf5da9219c3c8f1e3a6d0419`, then rejected the stale compiled pin as expected (12.402s Go, 18.755s wall). It is calibration evidence, not another behavioral RED. After pinning the exact observed fingerprint, `green-worker-lock` ran registration plus the authentic mixed-extension test successfully (67.043s Go, 73.230s wall). No predecessor pin changed.

The fix started from a new HEAD-only archive at `/tmp/zasp-scheduler64-fix1.9asP0D/source`. A fresh content/status/mode manifest records the same 2,235 unrelated dirty paths. The source gate froze three owned code/test files in `/tmp/zasp-scheduler64-fix1-gate.Yyv7a8/source`. ## Design decisions

1. Scheduler64 is separately checksummed and catalog-fingerprinted. Its dedicated Runner installs an immutable registration and forced-RLS tables without creating canonical migration row 64. The single worker-callable function checks exact scheduler64, worker63, public62, and release61 authority on every operation. Internal functions and tables stay owner-only.
2. Claim serializes global selection. It classifies eligibility before a deterministic, bounded oldest-eligible window, then revalidates the selected run under organization-first locks. It calls the unchanged retained-public and release61 orchestration authorities. Legacy and authentic non-admitted work are excluded; contradictory ordered history fails the entire call. No cursor, requeue, predecessor deletion, or predecessor state rewrite exists.
3. Scheduler, action, and deployment tokens are accepted only on requests. The scheduler stores separate SHA-256 digests, immutable worker bindings, and redacted projections. Stable live replay and every mutation require all original bindings. Heartbeat changes scheduler expiry/version only. A UTC-normalized evidence digest detects out-of-band changes to retained bindings, request, version, expiry, and projection before every scheduler call and before demotion. The state-only reconciled transition preserves that digest and every evidence field.
4. Recovery uses a genuinely new schedule identity after actual scheduler expiry and a locked read proving predecessor leases absent or expired. The old row is retained as expired, with its original identities, digests, request, and item. A trigger protects binding fields. Expired history permits only a state-only transition to reconciled after fresh reviewed clean-terminal proof. New scheduling never adopts a live action, deployment, child-test, reconciliation, or cleanup lease. First executor use remains the unchanged release61 reclaim/reconcile authority.
5. The approved pricing ruling is implemented as an immutable post-admission binding: exact historical policy/account rows, reviewed policy digest/validation, retained prepared request, settled provider reservation, and immutable admission response must agree. The scheduler does not call current pricing lookup after admission and cannot substitute a newer policy/account. Disable/rotation affects future planning, not admitted execution, stop, recovery, or cleanup.
6. Finish requires a genuine approval pause or clean terminal authority. The aggregate allowlist is exactly `contained`, `remediated`, `needs_human`, `cancelled`. A label alone is insufficient; clean terminal release cross-binds the fresh projection to retained reviewed transition/cleanup response evidence. Abandon before effects can release; retained durable intent is conservatively deferred until expiry. Release and finish end ownership by retaining a reconciled row, never deleting individual history. A separate eligibility-before-limit maintenance window reconciles expired clean history after a crash between predecessor completion and scheduler finish.
7. The Go boundary is package-private and typed. All caller-controlled identities, token formats, bounds, and versions are checked before I/O. Every operation uses exact compiled pins and one bounded SQL call. Decoding rejects missing, null, duplicate, extra, malformed, or contradictory fields and cross-checks canonical schedule/pricing IDs. Errors are mapped to fixed safe repository errors.
8. Down refuses any active, expired-unresolved, recovery-deferred, uncertain, or tampered scheduler history. Every row must be reconciled and pass a fresh locked predecessor/public proof that no runnable or unresolved policy/test/cleanup work remains. Only explicit verified demotion drops the extension table and its local audit history. Normal operation never deletes rows. Down/up replay restores exact predecessor catalog fingerprints, registrations, and canonical migration rows.

## Authentic fixture provenance

Successful scheduler PostgreSQL fixtures start with public62 activation and trigger, worker63 global planning claim, reviewed release61 prepare/start/result/settlement/artifact/admission, worker63 approval handoff, public62 approval, and reviewed progression. Owner writes seed configuration, identities, risk findings, and negative legacy inputs only. Owner mutations of authority are explicitly rolled-back refusal probes. Successful expiry tests wait for actual recorded deadlines; none advances a database lease clock.

Application fixtures use signed local policy envelopes and reviewed deployment claim/store/read/finish. Test fixtures use the reviewed artifact-bound dispatch and a controlled local HTTPS journal subprocess. Recovery verifies retained invocation/effect/reservation/cleanup identities and absence of duplicate receipts or sends. These are controlled local database/provider/artifact proofs, not deployed service or live external-provider proof.

## TDD record conventions

Each behavior was introduced after a named focused break and observed RED. Missing Go types, duplicate fixture roles, a wrong stop step, a wrong test regex, and fingerprint calibration failures are recorded as harness/calibration defects, not behavioral REDs. The initial abandon implementation was removed before its focused behavioral test; the retained implementation followed the observed abandon RED. Later regression tests that passed against an already-implemented general rule did not justify untested production behavior.

The command/output appendix records every captured RED/GREEN invocation and wall-clock duration. Catalog pin probes print the newly observed fingerprint, then intentionally fail the stale compiled-pin gate; they are calibration evidence, not product failures. Failed combined runs may contain useful individual GREENs, but are not reported as successful grouped gates.

## E2E2B handoff and limits

The post-admission runtime must not require live planner credential bytes or current pricing readiness merely to execute or clean admitted work. It must use the scheduler-bound original action/deployment identities while a schedule is live, and the unchanged release61 recovery authority on a fresh recovery schedule. The run-bound dormant runtime has not been composed or modified here. Independent review is mandatory before E2E2B.

E2E2B's mandatory first RED is `TestSecurityAgentRelease61CompositionPostgres`. Its existing config omits `Keys`, while the immutable constructor intentionally rejects `!c.Keys.Valid()` before database readiness. Repair that composition fixture and verify it when E2E2B owns composition; do not relax the constructor's signing-key preflight.

Final source fingerprint, frozen gate results, archive/reverse proof, exact owned-file manifest, dirty preservation checks, and complete command evidence are appended after verification.

## Demotion and restart proof

The authentic cleanup restart proof abandons a scheduler only after reviewed cleanup intent, waits for actual scheduler/action cleanup expiry, obtains a new schedule with new process identities and token digests, and invokes the unchanged release61 cleanup reconcile/claim path. Reclaim keeps the cleanup identity, increments its attempt, and does not create a receipt. The fixture then uses the new bound identities through reviewed signed deployment claim/store/read/finish and reviewed cleanup completion. Scheduler finish reconciles both current and expired rows. The old row is byte-for-byte unchanged after removing only its `state` field from comparison. No normal row deletion occurs.

Down refuses unresolved expired history. A rolled-back owner probe bypassing the immutability trigger and altering the retained action-token digest must return exact SQLSTATE `55000` with `scheduler ownership unresolved`. Valid, fully reconciled history permits down/up with exact predecessor fingerprints and canonical migration rows restored. A separate real-expiry case crashes after public cancellation but before scheduler finish; a fresh bounded claim returns empty while reconciling the clean history, after which verified demotion succeeds.

The first demotion implementation had a PL/pgSQL record/table-alias collision, diagnosed as `record "d" is not assigned yet`. That SQL defect is recorded as an implementation failure, not a successful refusal. The test was tightened to require the exact intended tamper-refusal error, and the corrected group passed in 155.472 seconds.

Application, test, cleanup, and deployment recovery all preserve reviewed predecessor identities and use actual recorded lease deadlines. Deployment separately proves that action/scheduler expiry is insufficient while the deployment lease remains live. Test uncertainty reconciliation retains one controlled journal invocation and no fabricated receipt. No path required a lost raw predecessor token to be stored or returned by scheduler64.

## Gate harness notes and limits

The frozen gate runs complete scheduler64 and worker63 suites, all public62-named repository/PostgreSQL groups, release61 runtime/orchestration/state groups, multistep application/progression/deployment groups, multistep test/cleanup/admission groups, full migrations, focused race, platform build, vet, formatting, whitespace, secret, archive/reverse, and dirty-preservation checks against one unchanged production/test snapshot.

The initial whitespace wrapper incorrectly treated the expected `git diff --no-index` new-file exit status 1 as a failure despite empty diagnostics. Only the external verification wrapper was corrected; frozen source did not change. Gitleaks reported three exact `generic-api-key` false positives on non-secret cancellation idempotency strings in tests: finish line 67, recovery line 136, and selection line 147. Each was inspected against frozen source. The reviewed scan fails any other finding; no secret was suppressed by a source annotation or broad path allowlist.

Global selection is intentionally serialized and eligibility inspection precedes bounded windows. The 101-plus fairness fixtures verify correctness, not production-scale throughput. These tests exercise local PostgreSQL, controlled providers, signed local artifacts, and a controlled HTTPS journal. They do not establish deployed or live external-provider behavior. Independent review remains required before E2E2B; no runtime/configuration composition was attempted.

During the two remaining predecessor groups, observed host UTC advanced from roughly `21:07` to `22:05` between status checks. Both test processes remained alive with their original 60-minute Go timeouts, and later fixtures continued. The wrapper records elapsed wall time with `Date.now()`, so those durations include this discontinuity. The host power log later confirmed clamshell sleep at `14:06:43 -0700` and full wake at `15:05:21 -0700`, with intervening short maintenance wakes. No process was interrupted by this task.

The first worker/public attempt exited 1: 58 root tests passed, one failed, and one parent-owned subprocess skipped. Its wall duration was 6695.228 seconds while Go reported 3247.784 seconds for the apiserver package. The only failure was unchanged `TestSecurityAgentWorker63FinishMatrixPostgres/cancelled/expired`, line 208, at the first expired handoff assertion before cancellation. The response was empty and the prior dispatch remained. The original disposable database had already been removed by fixture cleanup when buffered package output arrived, so its exact row timestamps cannot be recovered.

The single hypothesis was that host sleep advanced PostgreSQL wall time beyond the admitted plan's expiry, making the old waiting-approval run stop-required and correctly ineligible for worker63 handoff. The unchanged worker63 prefilter checks plan/budget expiry before handoff. An isolated unchanged rerun passed in 50.849 seconds. A second unchanged rerun with an external read-only observer passed in 47.723 seconds: its dispatch expired at `2026-09-22T15:16:38.289978-07:00`, admitted plan at `15:31:12.30818-07:00`, and budget at `16:16:07.921799-07:00`; the observed run moved from waiting_approval/version 3 to cancelled/version 4 after actual dispatch expiry. Observer wall/monotonic elapsed was 47685/47684 ms. This confirms normal timing and the sleep interval, but the specific failed-row stop classification remains an inference because that database is gone.

No source, fixture, expectation, lease, or clock was edited to make these retries pass. The failed whole-group output is retained, not counted as GREEN. Complete worker/public coverage is revalidated from the same frozen archive in three disjoint groups, whose union is checked against the original 60-root test selection. A focused retry alone does not satisfy the broad gate.

The complete unchanged worker63 finish matrix then passed in 610.360 seconds, including all ten progression/action-expired/cleanup-expired/rejected/cancelled live-and-expired cases. The previously failing cancelled/expired case passed in 44.88 seconds. This is whole-matrix retry evidence, not an edit to the fixture or its expected behavior.

### One authorized baseline exclusion

The initial release61/application attempt exited 1 after 7049.578 wall seconds; Go reported 3602.403 seconds and a 60-minute package timeout during `PartialTicksPostgres/deployment_read`. Before timeout, it recorded a sleep-overlapping `JournalTicksPostgres/journal_complete_expiry` failure (`stopped application_store`) and a separate earlier composition failure. The composition failure occurred before host sleep and is not classified as a timing incident.

`TestSecurityAgentRelease61CompositionPostgres` fails at line 37 because its line-35 config supplies no signing keys. `NewSecurityAgentRelease61Composition` rejects that config at line 29. The adjacent unit test deliberately verifies this rejection. An isolated frozen-source run reproduced the failure in 11.889 seconds; the exact restored base-only archive at `/tmp/zasp-scheduler64-reverse.o2MSFy/source`, with no scheduler64 files, reproduced it in 17.062 seconds. Both logs are retained below.

The parent explicitly authorized excluding exactly this test for E2E2A and required it as the first RED for E2E2B. No predecessor source or fixture was edited. The release61 retry ledger enumerates the original 64 root names, removes exactly `TestSecurityAgentRelease61CompositionPostgres`, and checks that four disjoint retry groups cover all remaining 63 roots. The partial timeout run is not counted as a passing gate. The worker/public retry ledger likewise covers all original 60 root names without exclusion. Every retry uses the unchanged frozen archive and independently records command, exit status, and timing.

### Commit boundary and remaining concerns

Only 14 new scheduler64 production/test files and this report are owned. The exact path set and SHA-256/mode/size manifest are in `gate-freeze`. Staging requires the original HEAD, an empty shared index, no existing shared owned paths, all ten passing gate categories, frozen code equality, and the original dirty manifest. It then copies and stages only those 15 paths, checks index bytes against the tested source, and reruns dirty-byte preservation. No push is performed.

The final document/staging/commit checks write `/tmp/zasp-scheduler64.VBDfE1/gate-final-document-reverse-verified.log`, `gate-final-report-quality-verified.log`, `gate-final-stage-verified.log`, and `gate-postcommit.log` after this report is frozen. They are not copied recursively back into the document whose exact bytes they verify. The postcommit check requires parent `c41b01b77e8ec8fc60b4486390e3232737bf2016`, exactly 15 committed paths, exact frozen code hashes, committed/report/source equality, an empty index, unchanged original dirty paths, and a clean archive of all 2,563 committed files.

The first final-report sync failed before copying because Node's default `execFileSync` output buffer was smaller than the 1.15 MB staged report. The following stage verification correctly rejected the stale report copy; no commit occurred. Only the external report-sync helper's buffer was increased to 16 MB. Frozen production/test source and expectations did not change. These administrative failures are retained below and are not product REDs or passing final staging evidence.

The baseline composition fixture remains mandatory first RED for E2E2B. Independent review is still required before runtime composition. Global serialized eligibility scans have correctness proof, including 101-plus fixtures, but no production-scale throughput benchmark. All external behavior here is controlled local database/provider/artifact/HTTPS proof, not deployed or live-provider proof. No release61 recovery path tested here required retaining or returning a lost raw token.
